name: Cākundi
location: From Dāinhāṭ station; a kroś and a half north of Agradvīpa, between Bardhamān and Nadīyā, a kroś and a half from Pāṭuli
about: The appearance place of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya Prabhu, and the śrīpāṭa of his father Gaṅgādhara Bhaṭṭācārya (Śrī Caitanya dāsa). Much of Cākundi has gone into the Gaṅgā and the village has moved, but many old marks remain. Śrīnivāsa Ācārya's samādhi was at Cākundi; it has now been moved. A festival is held here and at Jājigrāma on Kārtika Gopāṣṭamī.

name: Agradvīpa
location: Three kroś south of Kāṭwā; one kroś north of Agradvīpa Ghāṭ station
about: Govinda, Mādhava and Vāsudeva Ghoṣa lived here. The samādhi of Govinda Ghoṣa is at Agradvīpa; his house stood under a tree at Kāśīpura nearby, and his kinsmen still live there. According to the Kṣitīśa-vaṁśāvalī-carita (ch. 18), Govinda Ghoṣa Ṭhākura, a disciple of Śrī Caitanya who used to travel with him, installed the deity of Śrī Gopīnātha at Agradvīpa.

name: Bāghnāpāḍā
location: Bāghnāpāḍā station, the next after Kālnā on the Bārhāroyā loop line (Eastern Railway)
about: Śrīpāṭa of Vaṁśīvadana Ṭhākura and of Rāmāi Ṭhākura (Rāmacandra Gosvāmī).

name: Phuliyā
location: Four and a half kroś south-west of Rāṇāghāṭ; a mile from Phuliyā station (Śāntipura branch)
about: The śrīpāṭa of Haridāsa Ṭhākura. Kṛttivāsa Ojhā, the author of the Bengali Rāmāyaṇa, was born here on Śrī Pañcamī 1362 Śaka (11 February 1440).

name: Kāñcrāpāḍā
location: At the northern edge of 24 Parganas district
about: The śrīpāṭa of Vāsudeva Datta Ṭhākura. His family came from Chittagong; he lived first near Navadvīpa and later at Kāñcrāpāḍā in Nadīyā. He looked after the property of Śivānanda Sen. It was this Vāsudeva who said to Mahāprabhu: «Let me take the sins of all living beings and suffer in hell; deliver them all, O Lord.» Kāñcrāpāḍā was once in the kingdom of Rāja Pratāpāditya.

name: Buḍhan
location: In the Sātakṣīrā subdivision; reached from Khulnā towards Sātakṣīrā
about: The birthplace of Haridāsa Ṭhākura: a raised mound marks his home. Some say he was born in a brāhmaṇa family, his father named Sumati and his mother Gaurī; they died when he was a child, and the orphan Haridāsa was brought up in the house of the Khān sāhebs at Hālimpur, across the river from Buḍhan. According to Jayānanda his appearance place was Bhāṭ-kelāgāchi, two kroś from Buḍhan on the Sonāi.

name: Cātarā
location: A mile and a half from Śrīrāmapura station; the temple is in the Caudhurī-pāḍā
about: The śrīpāṭa and temple of Kāśīśvara Paṇḍita; also the śrīpāṭa of Śaṅkarāraṇya Paṇḍita. There are Nitāi-Gaura, Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, Sūrya-deva and a kuṇḍa; festivals at the Vāruṇī and at the Dola-yātrā.

name: Cāṁpāhāṭi
location: Two miles west of Navadvīpa; from Samudragaḍa station
about: The pāṭa of Dvija Vāṇīnātha, who in Vraja-līlā was the sakhī Kāmalekhā (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 204). The service of Śrī Gaura-Gadādhara, installed by Vāṇīnātha, continues here.
